record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Develop a satisfactory Lyapunov theory for linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators. This includes deciding whether ISS always implies the existence of a coercive or non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function, whether heat equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions admit coercive ISS Lyapunov functions, whether some linear ISS systems admit only non-coercive but not coercive ISS Lyapunov functions, and whether admissibility of the input operator can be characterized in Lyapunov terms.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.31. In spite of several positive results described in this section, our present knowledge of Lyapunov methods for linear systems with unbounded operators is insufficient, and many questions are open. The very first question is whether ISS of (3.1) implies the existence of a (coercive or non-coercive) ISS Lyapunov function.

It is known that for linear hyperbolic systems of conservation laws it is possible to construct a coercive ISS Lyapunov function [216], and at the time it is unknown, whether coercive ISS Lyapunov functions exist for a heat equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions, or, more generally, for systems governed by analytic semigroups generated by operators with an unbounded spectrum.

Also, it is not known whether there are linear ISS control systems for which there is no coercive ISS Lyapunov function, but non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions do exist. As ISS can be characterized as the exponential stability of a semigroup combined with the admissibility of the input operator, a Lyapunov characterization of the admissibility could probably be helpful.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a linear infinite-dimensional control system of the form
  ẋ(t) = A x(t) + B u(t),  x(0) = x₀ ∈ X,
where X is a Banach space, A: D(A) ⊂ X → X generates a strongly continuous semigroup (T(t))_{t≥0} on X, and B: U → X_{-1} is a (possibly unbounded) linear input operator with values in the extrapolation space X_{-1}, U being a Banach space of input values. Inputs u are taken from L^∞(0,∞;U) (or another suitable input space).

The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K such that for every initial state x₀ ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t; x₀, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_∞)   for all t ≥ 0.

A continuous functional V: X → [0,∞) is called a non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function if there exist α ∈ K_∞, ψ_2 ∈ K_∞, ρ ∈ K, and α_3 > 0 (or a positive definite α_3) such that
  ψ_1(‖x‖) ≤ V(x) ≤ ψ_2(‖x‖)   with ψ_1 only positive definite (not necessarily of class K_∞),
and the Dini derivative along trajectories satisfies V̇(x,u) ≤ −α_3(‖x‖) + ρ(‖u‖). It is called a coercive ISS Lyapunov function if additionally ψ_1 ∈ K_∞.

The operator B is called admissible (for (T(t))) if there exist t > 0 and c > 0 such that ∫₀^t T(t−s) B u(s) ds ∈ X with norm ≤ c‖u‖_{L^p(0,t;U)} for all u.

Address the following questions, providing proofs or counterexamples:
(a) Does ISS of the system always imply the existence of a (coercive or at least non-coercive) ISS Lyapunov function?
(b) Does the heat equation
  x_t = x_{xx} on (0,1), x(t,0) = u(t), x(t,1) = 0,
viewed as an ISS system in X = L^2(0,1) with Dirichlet boundary input, admit a coercive ISS Lyapunov function? More generally, do systems governed by analytic semigroups whose generators have unbounded spectrum admit coercive ISS Lyapunov functions?
(c) Do there exist linear ISS control systems with unbounded admissible input operators that admit non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions but no coercive ISS Lyapunov function?
(d) Can admissibility of the input operator B (relative to an exponentially stable semigroup) be characterized in terms of existence of an appropriate Lyapunov-type functional?
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on each sub-question but the program is not fully complete. Non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions for linear systems with unbounded admissible input operators (including the Dirichlet heat equation) were constructed by Jacob, Mironchenko, Partington, Wirth (SICON, 2020). Recent work on quadratic ISS Lyapunov functions for linear analytic systems (2023) and on coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals via the regular-systems framework (MCSS, 2025), as well as generalized Lyapunov functionals (Automatica, 2024), give positive answers for several classes including the Dirichlet heat equation, but a complete general Lyapunov theory and a Lyapunov characterization of admissibility remain not fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Noncoercive Lyapunov Functions for Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of noncoercive ISS Lyapunov functions for linear systems with unbounded admissible input operators, with application to the heat equation with Dirichlet boundary input.
status_evidence.claim: Non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions exist for the Dirichlet heat equation and related systems.

status_evidence.title: Coercive quadratic converse ISS Lyapunov theorems for linear analytic systems
status_evidence.snippet: For linear analytic systems, ISS does not imply the existence of a coercive quadratic Lyapunov function in general, but it does under contraction-similarity conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial negative/positive results regarding coercive quadratic ISS Lyapunov functions for analytic systems.

status_evidence.title: Coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular linear infinite-dimensional systems with applications.
status_evidence.claim: Coercive ISS Lyapunov functionals are now available for broad classes of regular linear systems.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Lyapunov functionals for the input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized Lyapunov functionals giving coercive ISS-type estimates for parabolic equations with Dirichlet boundary disturbances.
status_evidence.claim: Positive Lyapunov-functional results for the Dirichlet heat equation.
